findings.title: The Imaging screen's simulated capture still paints a random star field, so nothing captured under simulation can be plate-solved
findings.detail: S9 added a real-sky renderer (sim_sky.rs + sim_frame::synthesize_sim_frame) and wired it into device_manager/ops/camera.rs:1217, but the capture the Imaging screen actually performs goes through api/imaging.rs, whose `device_id.starts_with("sim_")` branch calls generate_simulated_image() (imaging.rs:1304-1344) - background + rand::thread_rng() stars at random positions with random brightness. Reproduced end to end on the release build with everything else correct: ASTAP + D05 detected and configured as catalog_path, sim camera + sim mount connected, optical train 1000mm f/5.0 giving 0.78"/px (the S9 probe solved sub-pixel at exactly this scale). ASTAP was handed the real FITS and searched +/-30 degrees around the mount position: '49 stars, 173 quads selected in the image ... No solution found!  :('. The app log never emits sim_sky's 'sim sky: indexed ... area files' line, confirming the sky index is never consulted on this path. Consequence: every plate-solve-gated surface stays unexercisable offline - the catalog overlay and its details panel, Slew & Center, screen:imaging/centering_dialog.dart, the framing wizard, mosaic tile solving, meridian-flip recentre and polar alignment's solve path - which is the opposite of what the closeout plan assumes now that sim_sky.rs has landed.
findings.fixSummary: Not fixed here: the fix is a Rust change plus a release rebuild of libskotiq_bridge.so, and eight other agents are driving the shared bundle right now, so rebuilding it mid-flight would break their runs. The confined fix is to have api/imaging.rs's simulator branch build a SimFrameRequest with sim_sky_view(...) and call synthesize_sim_frame, i.e. delete the second renderer rather than teach it about the sky.

findings.title: Auto-queue bright transients enforces a magnitude the app gives you no way to change
findings.detail: TransientAlertSettings.autoQueueMagnitude defaults to 10.0 and transient_alert_service.dart:771 gates auto-queueing on `alert.magnitude <= autoQueueMagnitude`. Most transients an amateur rig can actually reach sit at mag 13-17, so a hard 10.0 means the switch is effectively inert. The value is settable over the headless API (apps/desktop/lib/headless_api/handlers/transient_handlers.dart:144-158) and by TransientAlertSettingsNotifier.setAutoQueueMagnitude (transient_alert_provider.dart:362), which had zero UI callers; the only GUI reference printed it into a caption. Reproduced live: Plan Tonight > Recommendation > Transient Alerts > gear, toggled 'Auto-queue bright transients' to [ON] (confirmed in the a11y tree) and the dialog offered no threshold control at all, just the fixed 'Automatically add transients brighter than mag 10 to targets' subtitle.
findings.fixSummary: The Transient Alert Settings dialog now reveals a 5-20 magnitude slider (wired to the existing setAutoQueueMagnitude) whenever auto-queue is on, matching the display-threshold slider above it, plus a warning line when the auto-queue threshold is fainter than the feed's own magnitude threshold and therefore can never fire. New test packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/transients/transient_auto_queue_magnitude_test.dart covers all three states; it passes with the fix and 2 of its 3 cases fail when the fix is reverted.

findings.title: Settings search finds nothing for 'focal', the number that decides plate scale, framing and solving
findings.detail: Typing 'focal' into the Settings search box returns 'No settings match your search.' Focal length is not a Settings row - it lives in Equipment > Edit Profile > Optical Train - but a user hunting for it has no reason to know that, and the search that is otherwise the fastest way around the app dead-ends. Reproduced live on the release build; by contrast 'plate' correctly surfaces Plate Solving, Sequencer, Annotations, Notifications and Appliance Catalogs. The same applies to the other optical-train fields (aperture, reducer/barlow).
findings.fixSummary: Not fixed: the right answer is a product call between indexing equipment-profile fields into the settings search and adding cross-reference stubs that deep-link to Equipment > Edit Profile, and either would be a change to how the search index is defined rather than a confined edit.
